messages.subject: shinyapps.io to AWS postgreSQL connection.
messages.subject_clean: shinyapps.io to AWS postgreSQL connection.
messages.body_plain:
My shiny application connects just fine to my AWS postgreSQL instance from my local machine.  When deployed on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> the dbConnect command times out with:   'dial tcp 127.0.0.1:43954 <http://127.0.0.1:43954>: connection refused" and the program crashes.  I have had my administrator add the following IP address to AWS
> 54.204.37.78
> 54.204.29.251
> 54.204.36.75
> 54.204.34.9.

These are entries in the AWS authorization instances.   According to some prior posting here, I have even tried to load the older postgreSQL binaries  install.packages(RPostgreQSL, type= mac.binary).   No change.   Can still connect from my local machine but not from the deployed application.   I was reading that I might be required to make ssl keys on AWS and use a system() command in the R code on the shinyapp to get the shiny app to connect to AWS?

My shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> log appears to show that my PostgreSQL package is working.

Library(RPostgreSQL)

m<- dbDriver("PostgreSQL")
print(dbGetInfo(m))

This displays an object that looks identical on the shiny apps.io <http://apps.io> deployment and the local machine.

con<- dbConnect(m, user = "user",
password="password", host=  "xxx.xxx.us-east-1.rds.amazonaws.com <http://xxx.xxx.us-east-1.rds.amazonaws.com>" ,
port='5432'
dbname= 'dbname')

Crashes and displays the connection refused list above.

Could somebody please help?   Is creating SSL keys on AWS and executing system() commands from the deployed shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> the right direction?  See

https://support.rstudio.com/hc/communities/public/questions/203051837-How-to-Connect-to-External-Database-AWS-

messages.body_plain:
This is the ui.R

library(shiny)

shinyUI(fluidPage(
  fluidRow(

    column(4,

           # Copy the line below to make a slider range
           sliderInput("slider2", label = h3("Slider Range"), min = 0,
                       max = 100, value = c(-100, 100)),
           checkboxGroupInput("checkGroup", label = h3("Checkbox group"),
                              choices = list("A1" = "A1", "A2" = "A2", "B2" = "B2", "B4"="B4", "C9"="C9"),
                              selected = c("A1", "A2", "B2", "B4", "C9"))
    )
  ),

  hr(),

  fluidRow(
    DT::dataTableOutput('tbl')
  )

))

and this is the server.R

library(shiny)
library(DT)
library(dplyr)
set.seed(422015)
DF1 <- data.frame(V1=sample(x = c("A1", "A2", "B2", "B4", "C9"), size = 100, replace = T),
                  V2=runif(n = 100,min = -100, max = 100))
DF1 %>%
  group_by(V1) %>%
  summarise(mean=mean(V2)) %>%
  datatable()

shinyServer(function(input, output) {
  observe({

    output$tbl = renderDataTable({
      DF1 %>%
        filter(V2>input$slider2[1], V2<input$slider2[2],
               V1 %in% input$checkGroup) %>%
        group_by(V1) %>%
        summarise(mean=mean(V2)) %>%
        datatable(extensions = 'TableTools',
                  rownames = FALSE,
                  options = list(pageLength = 5, lengthMenu = c(5, 10, 15, 50, 100),
                                 dom = 'T<"clear">lfrtip',
                                 tableTools = list(sSwfPath = copySWF())
                  ))
    })

  })

})

Thanks!

for (f in seq(along = files)) {
  file <- file.path(folder, paste0(names(files)[f], ".R"))
  filecon <- file(file)
  writeLines(text = files[[f]], con = filecon)
  close(filecon)
}

devtools::install_github("rstudio/shinyapps")

messages.body_plain:
If the data is in a package, we are probably hitting a timeout while we try to download and install the package(s).  What packages are you looking for?

For uploads we have a limit of 100MB. We recognize that this is an issue that we will need to resolve for some users.
There are tricks to download the data sets before your application starts if the file is not there already, but I suspect those aren't helpful for this scenario.

messages.subject_clean: [shinyapps-users] Uploading files to shinyapps
messages.body_plain:
The file that the customer uploads will be on the server while the application is up for that user.  To be safe you should treat that storage as transient, ie. if you redeploy your application, or if we migrate your application from one server to another the storage that was used by the customer wouldn't be carried across.

Hope that answers your question.

messages.body_plain:
Thanks, Tareef.  I was figuring out the answer when your reply came in.  For anyone else trying to make plotly and shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> work together, this is what I did:
clone the rOpenSci/plotly repo into your Shiny app directory (alongside server.R, ui.R, and any helper files)
in plotly/R/tools.R, change the tilde (~) in line 3 to '.', i.e., PLOTLY_DIR <- file.path(path.expand("."), ".plotly")
install package IRdisplay using devtools::install_github("IRkernel/IRdisplay")
rather than using library(plotly) or require(plotly), source the .R files in ./plotly/R/;
bring in the packages that plotly uses with library/require, which includes the following packages: RCurl, RJSONIO, lattice, xtable, and httr.
deploy to shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>
Jacob

messages.subject: Problem when reloading an animated GIF in Chrome
messages.subject_clean: Problem when reloading an animated GIF in Chrome
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I'm facing a strange problem when reloading an animated GIF that only shows when using Google Chrome (Firefox and Internet Explorer don't show the problem). I've tested it in Chrome 42.0.2311.90, Firefox 37.0.1 and Internet Explorer 9.0.8112.16421

I want to include an animated GIF that shows a 1-second animation (it does not loop forever, i.e. it shows the animation and ends) in my Shiny application. More specifically, I want to show the animation every time an action button is pressed.

I have included in my ui.R file an imageOutput ("animated_image", the placeholder for the animated gif) and the corresponding actionButton ("show").

Then I have included the following code in my server.R file:

output$animated_image <- renderImage({
    input$show
    list(src="www/anim_1.gif")
}, deleteFile = FALSE)

when I load the application on Chrome, the animation only runs once (the first time the code is run). After that, whenever I press the button the image stays the same, just showing the last frame of the animated GIF. However, if I load it on Firefox or IE the application behaves as desired, i.e. the animation runs each time I press the button.

Fearing some problem related with image caching, I created a second version of the animated GIF with a slight modification in some pixels (so that it doesn't identify it as the same file) and stored it as "anim_2.gif". After that, I modified the code so that it loads alternatively the 1st or the 2nd version, hoping that the browser sees it as a different image than the previous one. This is the code (variable COUNT is previously initialized with 0):

output$animate_image <- renderImage({
    COUNT <- COUNT + input$show
    if (COUNT %% 2 == 0){filename="www/anim_1.gif"}
        else {filename="www/anim_2.gif"}
    list(src=filename)
}, deleteFile = FALSE)

In this case, the animation runs just twice (the first time the code is run, and after pressing the button for the first time). After that, it seems like Chrome detects that I'm trying to load an image that has already been loaded before (even if it is not the immediate previous one) and "refuses" to load the animation again. Firefox and IE still work fine.

I've also tried some solutions I found for related problems in other contexts, e.g. adding a random number as an additional parameter in the URL, like this:

list(src=paste0("www/anim_1.gif?x=",abs(rnorm(1))))

but that doesn't work in this case, as Shiny can't find the image with that tweaked URL.

Any ideas on how can I solve this problem that only shows in Chrome?

Thanks,
Mikel

messages.subject: Setting up users for only viewing - not account management
messages.subject_clean: Setting up users for only viewing - not account management
messages.body_plain:
I was curious how on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> I can create user accounts that only allow authentication to access an apps' URL. In other words, I don't want the user to be able to view any of the actual account details. Even better, can I create users and their passwords without the system having to email that person? Eventually I see a scenario where I want to have perhaps 25 total users but it'd be great to create the accounts for them and apply the permissions by application.

Thanks!

messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] Setting up users for only viewing - not account management
messages.subject_clean: [shinyapps-users] Setting up users for only viewing - not account management
messages.body_plain:
Adding a user as an authorized user to an application (under the "Users" tab) will create a User Profile on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>, but will not give them access to deploy or manage applications within your shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> account (logging in to the dashboard will not show the application details either). This feature is possible with the Standard plan and above. The professional plan allows you to add users to your account, giving them full access to deploy/manage/view all applications within that account, and will show the application details just as you see it for your own account).

We do have work on our backlog to allow you to do two things a) manage users via the shinyapps package.  2) send custom emails, or no emails when you add a user to an application, but it will still require them to create an shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> User Profile and set their own password or other authentication mechanism (Google/GitHub/etc).

Hope that helps.
-Andy

messages.subject: Shiny takes over RStudio
messages.subject_clean: Shiny takes over RStudio
messages.body_plain:
Hi folks,

Sorry for asking a bit of a nOOb question, but I'm having some workflow issues regarding Shiny and RStudio.

I have been building an application (and having lots of fun doing so) in RStudio, but wanted to take a break to work in a normal R session. I hit 'Esc' to do so, and I've found that I can run code in separate R files without much of an issue.

But I am also in the habit of using the Ctrl-Alt-R command in order to run a whole .R file (to see whether my output is reproducible, etc.). Ever since I started working on that Shiny App, however, Ctrl-Alt-R automatically runs the ShinyApp I was building. I have tried hitting Esc multiple times, clearing my workspace, terminating/restarting R, and even closing and exiting RStudio.

 I'm not sure what I'm missing, but any help would be greatly appreciated. Thank you.

best,
Daanoo

messages.subject_clean: Shiny takes over RStudio
messages.body_plain:
Sorry, I figured out the problem. In case anyone else benefits from this: RStudio anticipates that you're working on an app, whenever you are working on a different R file within the directory that hosts your ui.R and server.R files, for the app. Even if the files are unrelated. Maybe it's bad form, on my part, to have other files in this same folder.

Ctrl-Alt-R behaviour works, as normal, when you're working on .R files that aren't in a folder with ui.R and server.R files

messages.body_plain:
Hi Tareef,

I encountered a similar issue and your approach worked -- thank you for the walk-trough. However, there was a problem others may encounter also:

The default Startup Timeout may be insufficient to download large datasets. Specifically, it was insufficient for ~250Mb download and start-up in my case. Even the 300-sec. maximum could be too low to download and load datasets near 1Gb, depending on the source.

In the end, it would be great to have a more direct path for deploying large datasets.

Thank you and good luck working on the more elegant solution,
Greg

Aaron,

I believe what you want is currently supported. Let me explain further:

If you visit the "Users" page under your application page in the shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> dashboard, you will be able to add users who will ONLY be able to VIEW that particular application.

If you visit the "Members" age under "Account" in the shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> dashboard, you will be able to add users who will be able VIEW and MANAGE all applications in the account.

Let me know if this is not what you are looking for.
-Andy

messages.subject_clean: Poor ShinyApp performance
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I'm enrolled in Coursera's Data Science Specialization, currently working in the Capstone Project. I have uploaded a text prediction tool to ShinyApps but the performance is considerably poor. Normally, I would blame myself :), but when I run it from R Studio I get predictions in less than 5 seconds... however with the online version, I can sometimes get one prediction and then the app hangs when I retry or it just hangs in the first prediction (and I mean it REALLY hangs, the browser doesn't even refreshes or just tells me to "please wait" forever.

I have a free account, and I know that there are some resources limitations... however I still have less than 20 hours of usage (out of which it has never worked, but let's not go there), and my profile's performance monitors show that I have never reached the 500MB memory usage limit.

Is there something I can check in my profile or my code? or is this something that needs to be looked at from the architecture perspective?

link to my app: https://dabergueiro.shinyapps.io/CapstoneProject/

 <https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/-XE2IbrUWHNA/VTgFn6GFFzI/AAAAAAAABrg/8YIkOYBLJ3s/s1600/ShinyApps%2Bperf.JPG>

FYI, since R 3.2.0, there is a cross-platform method to read https
resources, which is to use a url() connection with the libcurl method,
e.g.

con = url('http://raw.githubusercontent.com/shirley-wang/STAT-480/613aec9f37e4042614edaada2bac1b5c855e8bcb/SpeedDating%20-%20Copy.csv',
method = 'libcurl')
x = read.csv(con)
str(x)

The OP was using R 3.1.3, so this method would not work.

Regards,
Yihui
